learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the family of four-sided shapes! Learn the unique properties of parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, and squares, and how they relate.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: समद्विभाजित करना (दो बराबर भागों में काटना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If you draw a diagonal inside any quadrilateral, it splits into two triangles. Since a triangle's angles add up to 180°, the interior angles of ANY quadrilateral must always add up to exactly 360° ($180^\circ \times 2$).

A parallelogram is a shape where opposite sides are parallel. Because of this, magic happens: Opposite sides become equal, opposite angles become equal, and their diagonals perfectly bisect (cut each other in half)!
A Rectangle is a parallelogram with 90° angles. A Rhombus is a parallelogram with all 4 sides equal. A Square is the king—it is a rectangle AND a rhombus combined (90° angles AND equal sides)!
If you mark the exact mid-points of two sides of a triangle and draw a line connecting them, that new line will be perfectly parallel to the third side, and exactly HALF its length!

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The 360° Paper Tear
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a large, irregular quadrilateral on a piece of paper. Color its 4 inside corners. Now, tear off all 4 corners and arrange the colored points so they touch. They will form a perfect, continuous circle, proving the angles add up to exactly 360°!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize diagonal properties: In a Parallelogram they just bisect. In a Rectangle, they are EQUAL. In a Rhombus, they cross at exactly 90° (perpendicular). A Square does all three!
📌 Every Square is a Rectangle and a Rhombus, but a Rectangle is NOT necessarily a Square. Be careful with 'True/False' questions on this.
📌 The Mid-Point Theorem is highly tested in proofs. Look for triangles inside quadrilaterals to apply it.
quick_recap: ⭐ The sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral is always 360°.
⭐ A parallelogram features equal and parallel opposite sides and bisecting diagonals.
⭐ The Mid-Point theorem links the midpoints of a triangle to its third side in length and parallel direction.
